title: mentha arvensis subsp. haplocalyx
intro: Mentha arvensis subsp. haplocalyx, commonly known as Chinese wild mint or Japanese peppermint, is a subspecies of the wild mint plant native to East Asia. It has been used in traditional medicine for its various health benefits, which include reducing inflammation, relieving digestive issues, and exhibiting antimicrobial properties. The therapeutic actions of M. arvensis subsp. haplocalyx are attributed to its bioactive constituents, such as menthone, limonene, and beta-pinene, which have been shown to exhibit anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antiseptic properties. Additionally, the plant's essential oil has been used to treat respiratory issues, such as bronchitis and asthma, due to its expectorant and bronchodilatory actions.
